result.title: WordInferBench: Can Agents Infer How to Edit from Word Document Context?
result.summary: Document editing is among the most common knowledge-work tasks, yet existing benchmarks for evaluating autonomous agents on Word document editing provide fully specified attribute-modification instructions. They do not evaluate agents' ability to infer the appropriate attributes from document context, a capability essential in real-world editing where users expect consistency without spelling out every attribute. We introduce WordInferBench, a benchmark comprising 280 base document-editing instances, each paired with three instruction conditions: descriptive (the instruction explicitly lists every attribute change), referential (the instruction points to another object as an exemplar), and inferential (the agent must examine document context to infer what attributes to apply). To evaluate contextual attribute inference, each base instance is constructed so that the target formatting is recoverable from an in-document exemplar. The instances are derived from real Word documents collected from Common Crawl and cover 13 object types and 81 attributes. We evaluate six recent coding-agent systems and find that the best-performing evaluated system, Claude Code with Opus 4.6, achieves a 62.9% task-level pass rate on descriptive variants but only 40.7% on inferential variants, indicating that current systems complete tasks less reliably when the required formatting changes must be determined from document context.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 WordInferBench：280 个真实 Word 文档编辑实例，各配描述式、指称式、推断式三种指令，覆盖 13 类对象与 81 个属性，并评测六个 coding agent，发现推断式通过率（40.7%）明显低于描述式（62.9%）。
AI.relevance_reason: 「须从文档上下文中推断未明示的必要属性」与 LVR 关注的视觉证据筛选、任务必要信息获取在问题表述上相通，但该工作无视觉输入与 latent 状态分析，可能仅供核查上下文推断任务的设计与缺口。
